title: Below-Knee Prosthesis
desc: A precision-engineered modular assistive mobility device featuring a pneumatic adaptive socket and micro-adjustable height calibration — designed to give amputees a fully personalized, comfortable lower limb replacement.

report.overview: The Modular Below-Knee Prosthesis is a 70-part precision assembly that prioritizes individual adaptability at every level — from micro-adjustable length calibration to a pneumatically adaptive socket that dynamically conforms to each user's residual limb anatomy. It balances full weight-bearing structural demands with the modularity needed for long-term personalization.
report.principle: Two integrated mechanisms work in parallel: a precision screw-thread length adjustment system for fine height calibration, and an inflatable pneumatic bladder in the socket that expands to fill the exact contour of the residual limb. Together they ensure a precise macroscopic and microscopic fit — accommodating daily limb volume fluctuations without clinical refitting.

components.name: Prosthetic Socket (Upper Frame)
components.desc: The primary interface between the residual limb and the prosthetic structure, transferring all weight-bearing loads. Designed to house the internal pneumatic bladder system.

components.name: Pneumatic Inflatable Bladder
components.desc: A flexible airtight lining inside the socket walls. When inflated, it expands inward to fill the precise limb contours — eliminating gaps, pressure points, and pistoning motion.

components.name: Inflation Valve & Pump Mechanism
components.desc: A compact air management system giving the user direct real-time control over socket tightness throughout the day.

components.name: Screw-Thread Length Adjustment
components.desc: A precision threaded mechanism allowing fine height calibration of the prosthesis for perfect bilateral limb symmetry, optimizing gait, posture, and spinal alignment.

components.name: Locking Collar & Retention Nut
components.desc: Clamps the threaded length mechanism firmly once the desired adjustment is reached — critical for structural safety under dynamic loading.

components.name: Structural Pylon (Central Shaft)
components.desc: The primary load-bearing column transmitting compressive forces from socket to foot. Engineered for axial stiffness, fatigue resistance, and minimal weight.

components.name: Ankle-Foot Assembly
components.desc: The terminal element interfacing with the ground — replicating natural ankle mechanics with energy return at push-off, shock absorption at heel strike, and stable surface contact.

components.name: Connector Adapters & Coupling Joints
components.desc: Standardized modular interfaces between socket, pylon, and foot allowing individual replacement or upgrade without replacing the full device.

components.name: Alignment Adjustment Joints
components.desc: Multi-axis elements between pylon and foot allowing angular fine-tuning to distribute ground reaction forces correctly and optimize gait efficiency.

components.name: Protective Outer Shell
components.desc: A shaped outer casing protecting internal mechanics from dust, moisture, and impact while providing an aesthetically appropriate external appearance.

components.name: Fasteners, Bearings & Hardware
components.desc: The complete set of 70 precision bolts, nuts, bearing elements, seals, and retaining components maintaining alignment and long-term reliability under cyclic loading.

features: Pneumatic adaptive fit — dynamically conforms to residual limb volume
Micro-adjustable height calibration for bilateral symmetry
User-controlled comfort — no clinical intervention needed
Modular architecture — replace components without replacing the device
Full weight-bearing structural integrity across 70 precision parts

title: Supercharged V12 Engine
desc: A 897-part fully detailed Supercharged V12 Internal Combustion Engine — one of the most prestigious engine configurations ever built. Twin banks of six cylinders, DOHC four-camshaft layout, forced induction supercharger, and equal-length exhaust headers.

report.overview: The Supercharged V12 is a 897-part assembly representing the pinnacle of automotive engineering sophistication. With 12 cylinders in two banks of six at a 60° V-angle, it delivers exceptional power, near-zero vibration, and the signature smooth linear power curve that defines V12 character. The supercharger adds 30–100% additional power over natural aspiration.
report.principle: The V12 operates on the four-stroke Otto cycle across 12 cylinders firing every 60° of crankshaft rotation — producing an almost perfectly continuous power delivery with exceptionally low vibration. The supercharger forces additional compressed air into the combustion chambers, dramatically increasing air-fuel charge density and power output.

components.name: Engine Block (V-Configuration)
components.desc: Central structural foundation housing 12 cylinder bores in two banks of six at 60°, providing near-perfect primary and secondary balance without a balance shaft.

components.name: Cylinder Heads (×2)
components.desc: Two separate DOHC heads atop each bank, each containing combustion chambers, valve seats, valve guides, coolant passages, and multi-valve configuration.

components.name: Supercharger (Twin-Screw)
components.desc: The visually dominant forced induction unit mounted centrally on top of the intake manifold, feeding pressurized air through dual inlets to increase power density dramatically.

components.name: Intake Manifold
components.desc: Distributes the pressurized air-fuel mixture evenly across all 12 cylinders with geometry optimized for equal charge distribution and minimal pressure drop.

components.name: Exhaust Headers (×2 Banks)
components.desc: Equal-length tubular headers — six per bank — ensuring each cylinder's exhaust pulse assists scavenging for maximum volumetric efficiency and power.

components.name: Timing System & Camshaft Drive
components.desc: Toothed belt and sprocket assembly driving four camshafts in precise synchronization with the crankshaft — two per cylinder bank.

components.name: Crankshaft
components.desc: Forged steel crankshaft running the full block length, converting the reciprocating motion of 12 pistons into rotational output with precisely calculated counterweights.

components.name: Pistons, Connecting Rods & Valvetrain
components.desc: 12 forged pistons with high-strength connecting rods, plus the full camshaft, tappet, rocker arm, and valve assembly managing gas exchange across all cylinders.

components.name: Accessory Drive System
components.desc: Belt-driven pulley system powering auxiliary components including alternator, water pump, power steering pump, and supercharger drive from the crankshaft snout.

components.name: Cooling & Lubrication Systems
components.desc: Integrated coolant passages and high-volume oil pump circulating pressurized lubricant to all bearing surfaces, camshafts, and valvetrain under extreme supercharged loads.

features: 897-part production-grade complexity and full mechanical fidelity
12-cylinder balance — near-zero vibration from perfect force cancellation
Forced induction supercharger — dramatically elevated power density
Equal-length exhaust headers for maximum scavenging efficiency
DOHC four-camshaft configuration for precise 12-cylinder valve timing

title: V6 Engine Assembly
desc: A detailed V6 internal combustion engine assembly showcasing the six-cylinder V-configuration powerplant — the backbone of performance sedans, sports cars, and modern SUVs worldwide. A study in compact power and engineering balance.

report.overview: The V6 engine represents the perfect middle ground between four-cylinder efficiency and eight-cylinder power. With six cylinders arranged in two banks of three, it delivers a compelling balance of compact packaging, smooth operation, and strong power output — making it the most widely used performance engine configuration across the global automotive industry.
report.principle: Operating on the four-stroke cycle, six cylinders fire in a carefully timed sequence to produce smooth, overlapping power strokes. The V-configuration allows a significantly shorter engine length compared to an inline-six while maintaining excellent inherent balance, contributing to both structural rigidity and refined NVH (noise, vibration, harshness) characteristics.

components.name: Engine Block (V6 Configuration)
components.desc: Central structural housing for six cylinder bores arranged in two banks of three — providing a compact, stiff structure ideal for transverse or longitudinal mounting.

components.name: Cylinder Heads (×2)
components.desc: One head per cylinder bank, each containing combustion chambers, intake and exhaust ports, valve seats, and coolant passages.

components.name: Crankshaft
components.desc: A five-main-bearing or four-main-bearing forged crankshaft converting six pistons' reciprocating motion into rotational output with balanced counterweights.

components.name: Pistons & Connecting Rods
components.desc: Six forged aluminum pistons connected via steel connecting rods translating combustion pressure into torque at the crankshaft.

components.name: Valvetrain (DOHC / SOHC)
components.desc: Camshaft-driven intake and exhaust valves controlling the gas exchange process across all six cylinders with precise timing.

components.name: Intake Manifold
components.desc: Distributes the incoming air-fuel mixture or air charge evenly across all six cylinders for balanced combustion and power output.

components.name: Exhaust System
components.desc: Tubular exhaust headers collecting combustion gases from each cylinder and routing them to the collector and downstream exhaust system.

components.name: Timing System
components.desc: Belt or chain-driven timing system synchronizing crankshaft and camshaft rotation to maintain correct valve timing throughout the engine's operating range.

components.name: Cooling & Lubrication
components.desc: Integrated water jacket coolant passages and pressurized oil lubrication system maintaining thermal and mechanical integrity under full load.

features: Compact V6 packaging — shorter than inline-six with superior rigidity
Smooth power delivery from overlapping six-cylinder firing sequence
Balanced V-configuration — excellent inherent primary force cancellation
Versatile mounting — suits transverse FWD or longitudinal RWD layouts
Widely deployed in performance sedans, SUVs, and sports cars globally

title: Wankel Rotary Engine
desc: The legendary Wankel Rotary Engine — a triangular rotor spinning inside an epitrochoidal housing, achieving the complete four-stroke combustion cycle through pure rotational motion. Made famous by Mazda's iconic RX-7 and RX-8, it is one of the most intellectually distinctive mechanical concepts in automotive history.

report.overview: The Wankel Engine fundamentally reimagines internal combustion by replacing reciprocating pistons with a continuously rotating triangular rotor. Invented by Felix Wankel in the 1950s and famously commercialized by Mazda in the RX-7 and RX-8, it delivers an exceptionally compact, lightweight, and high-revving power unit with a remarkably smooth power delivery character that no conventional piston engine can replicate.
report.principle: A three-sided Reuleaux triangular rotor orbits within a two-lobed epitrochoidal housing — a mathematically derived shape that maintains perfect sealing contact at all times. Each of the rotor's three faces simultaneously performs a different combustion phase, producing three power strokes per rotor revolution — far more frequent than a four-stroke piston engine — delivering exceptional smoothness and continuous torque.

components.name: Epitrochoidal Housing (Rotor Housing)
components.desc: A precisely machined oval chamber following a two-lobed epitrochoidal curve — ensuring the three apex seals maintain continuous contact throughout full rotation to create three isolated combustion chambers.

components.name: Triangular Rotor
components.desc: The heart of the engine — a three-sided rotor with concave faces serving simultaneously as piston faces for three combustion chambers. Its internal gear meshes with the stationary gear enforcing the 3:1 orbital-to-rotation ratio.

components.name: Eccentric Shaft (Output Shaft)
components.desc: The functional crankshaft equivalent — directly receiving orbital rotational energy from the rotor and delivering final power output at three times the rotor's orbital frequency.

components.name: Front & Rear Side Housings
components.desc: Precision-flat end plates sandwiching the rotor housing, carrying the stationary gear, coolant passages, oil seals, and mounting faces for intake and exhaust ports.

components.name: Apex Seals
components.desc: Three spring-loaded seal blades at each rotor tip — the most mechanically critical components. They maintain gas-tight chamber division as they slide continuously along the housing at high speed.

components.name: Side Seals & Corner Seals
components.desc: Flat sealing elements on rotor side faces preventing axial gas and oil leakage, with corner seals bridging the junction between apex and side seals.

components.name: Spark Plugs (Dual per Rotor)
components.desc: Two plugs per rotor — leading and trailing — required because the elongated crescent-shaped combustion chamber cannot be reliably ignited by a single plug at high RPM.

components.name: Internal Rotor Gear & Stationary Gear
components.desc: A matched gear pair enforcing the precise 3:1 geometric ratio governing rotor orbital motion — ensuring apex seals never lose contact with the housing wall.

components.name: Intake & Exhaust Ports
components.desc: Fixed ports opened and closed by the passing rotor edges — eliminating the entire valve train mechanism, contributing to the engine's high-RPM capability and mechanical simplicity.

components.name: Cooling & Lubrication System
components.desc: Coolant passages cast into the housing plus metered oil injection into the intake charge for apex seal lubrication — a design necessity contributing to the engine's characteristic oil consumption.

features: Zero reciprocating mass — no vibration at source, exceptionally smooth power
Three power strokes per rotor revolution — continuous torque output
Radically compact packaging — far smaller than equivalent piston engines
No valve train — fixed ports eliminate camshafts, valves, and springs entirely
Iconic motorsport legacy — Mazda RX-7, RX-8, and 24h Le Mans victories
